'''Derek Matthew Anderson''' (born June 15, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]]. Anderson was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the sixth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. A 2007 [[Pro Bowl]]er, he also played for the [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Carolina Panthers]], and [[Buffalo Bills]].

==Early life==
Anderson grew up in [[Scappoose, Oregon]], where he led the Scappoose Indians [[high school football|football]] team to one of their record three consecutive state football championships in Class 3A football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arnold |first=Geoffrey |date=February 4, 2016 |title=Derek Anderson, the former Beavers QB and a Scappoose native, happy as Cam Newton's backup |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/nfl/index.ssf/2016/02/ex-osu_qb_derek_anderson_happy.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=OregonLive.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He excelled at [[basketball]] and was named state player of the year in both football and basketball his senior year. He participated in the first ever [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] game in 2000. He was a childhood friend and schoolmate of Playboy Playmate [[Sara Jean Underwood]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garber |first=Greg |date=December 27, 2007 |title=Derek Anderson: From humble beginnings to budding star |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=garber_greg&id=3161910 |access-date=March 16, 2010 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
A Beaver fan growing up, Anderson wanted to play for [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] most of his life, and his decision as a top national prospect to play for the Beavers was celebrated by fans.

At 6-feet-6-inches, many believed Anderson would play basketball in college. Despite his stature, Anderson was highly recruited nationally for football, especially after his dominating senior year performance in high school as quarterback.

===Freshman season (2001)===
As a freshman in the [[2001 Oregon State Beavers football team|2001 season]], Anderson appeared in five games and recorded 263 passing yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Anderson 2001 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/derek-anderson-1/gamelog/2001/ |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Sophomore season (2002)===
Anderson's early entry as the starting quarterback came on the heels of Oregon State's most successful period to date. Capped by a crushing 41–9 [[2001 Fiesta Bowl|Fiesta Bowl]] win over [[2000 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]], the team went 11–1 in [[2000 Oregon State Beavers football team|2000]] and ranked 4th in the nation under [[head coach]] [[Dennis Erickson]]. Following the breakthrough season, fan expectations were exceptionally high in 2002 for the Oregon State program to pick up where they left off.

Unfortunately, Oregon State had lost the majority of its star players to the NFL in [[2001 NFL draft|2001]] and the inexperienced Anderson was handed the reins of a team many overestimated and believed would again crack the top 25. However, the team's youth was easily apparent from the start and led to a string of early losses. Still, Anderson and the team's performance rapidly improved and the Beavers recorded an 8–5 season.<ref>{{Citation |title=2002 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/2002-schedule.html |work=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref> He and the team's work were good enough to give them entry into the [[2002 Insight Bowl]], against the [[2002 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|University of Pittsburgh]]. Oregon State lost 38–13 and coach Erickson left for an NFL head-coaching position with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Insight Bowl – Pitt vs Oregon State Box Score, December 26, 2002 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2002-12-26-oregon-state.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Junior season (2003)===
Pressures on the team to repeat the program's 2000 performance were compounded by the coaching change at the end of 2002–2003. The return of previous head coach [[Mike Riley (American football)|Mike Riley]] from the [[NFL]] meant learning an entirely new system. With help from teammate and star running back [[Steven Jackson]], Anderson again rose to the occasion and played a leading role in propelling the team to an 8–5 record, capped by a 55–14 [[2003 Las Vegas Bowl|Las Vegas Bowl]] win over a then up-and-coming [[New Mexico Lobos football|New Mexico]] program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/2003-schedule.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Las Vegas Bowl – Oregon State vs New Mexico Box Score, December 24, 2003 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2003-12-24-new-mexico.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Senior season (2004)===
Throughout the [[2004 Oregon State Beavers football team|2004 season]], Anderson surprised many defenses with his ability to escape the tackle and run the ball effectively. He became a dual-threat quarterback and began showing a true command of the game by his improvisation in the pocket and successful outlet passing when under duress. Although the team's 7–5 performance was far from spectacular, Anderson became nationally recognized as a dangerous offensive weapon who could strike long gains at will.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2004 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/2004-schedule.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Beavers were without Steven Jackson, who was [[2004 NFL draft|drafted into the NFL]] the previous spring. Even without the star running back, Anderson led his team back to the [[2004 Insight Bowl|Insight Bowl]] where they again faced [[2004 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]] (led by Anderson's future Browns teammate [[Brady Quinn]]). The Beavers never trailed in the game and defeated the Irish 38–21. Anderson passed for 359 yards and had four touchdown passes with no interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Insight Bowl – Oregon State vs Notre Dame Box Score, December 28, 2004 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-12-28-notre-dame.html |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Anderson is the fourth player in [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10]] history to throw for over 4,000 yards in a single season, setting an Oregon State record at 4,058 yards in the [[2003 Oregon State Beavers football team|2003 season]]. He ranks second in the [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10]] for career touchdown passes, at 79 (also an Oregon State record). He is the 6th person ever to throw for 10,000 yards in a career in the Pac-10.

===Baltimore Ravens===
Anderson was selected out of [[Oregon State University]] by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the sixth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]] (213th overall).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=May 7, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He never played for them and was waived on September 20, 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Preston |first=Mike |date=November 1, 2007 |title=McAlister is key to locking up receivers |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2007/11/02/mcalister-is-key-to-locking-up-receivers/ |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=Baltimore Sun}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===

====2005 season====
Anderson was claimed off [[Waivers (American football)|waivers]] by the [[Cleveland Browns]] the day after being waived by the Ravens.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pasquarelli |first=Len |date=December 15, 2006 |title=Anderson to start for Browns; Frye still has sore wrist |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2698797 |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He did not see any action, being third on the depth chart behind [[Trent Dilfer]] and [[Charlie Frye]].{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

====2006 season====
Anderson served as Frye's backup for the Cleveland Browns in 2006 season. He made his NFL debut against the [[2006 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] at [[Cleveland Browns Stadium]], on October 22, taking one snap after Frye was briefly shaken up.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Cleveland Browns – October 22nd, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610220cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His second NFL appearance was more noteworthy. After Frye injured his wrist during the first half of Cleveland's December 3 game against the [[2006 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]], Anderson played the entire second half. He threw his first two NFL touchdowns in that game, connecting with [[tight end]] [[Steve Heiden]] twice in the fourth quarter. Anderson scrambled for 33 yards in overtime, moving the ball from the Kansas City 45-yard line to the 12-yard line, after which the Browns were in [[Field goal (football)|field goal]] range. His play was instrumental in leading the Browns back from a 28–14 deficit to a 31–28 overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Cleveland Browns – December 3rd, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612030cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> 
Overall, Anderson appeared in five games and recorded 793 passing yards, five touchdowns, and eight interceptions in the 2006 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Anderson 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeDe00/gamelog/2006/ |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2007 season====
Although some reports said he outplayed incumbent starter Frye and rookie [[Brady Quinn]] in minicamp, Anderson was not as productive in the pre-season games and Frye was named the starter for the [[2007 NFL season|2007 season]]. Head coach [[Romeo Crennel]] earlier said that the two were so close in effectiveness that he would use a [[coin toss]] to decide which quarterback would start the first preseason game. Anderson would take over for Frye in the 2007 opener after Frye was ineffective in the first quarter against the Browns' archrival, the [[2007 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns – September 9th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709090cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The game was Frye's last in a Browns uniform, as he was traded to the [[Seattle Seahawks]] for a sixth-round draft pick two days later. Named the starting quarterback by Crennel for Week 2, Anderson threw for 328 yards and five touchdowns against the [[2007 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] in his first start. His [[passer rating]] for the game was 121.0 as the Browns defeated the Bengals 51–45, solidifying Anderson's role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Cleveland Browns – September 16th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709160cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the same game, Bengals quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] threw for six touchdown passes. It was only the third time in NFL history that two quarterbacks had thrown at least five touchdown passes in the same game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morona |first=Joey |date=September 17, 2007 |title=Browns 51, Bengals 45 (Yes, that's 51 points) |url=https://www.cleveland.com/sports/2007/09/browns_51_bengals_45_yes_thats.html |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=cleveland.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 30, Anderson beat the team that drafted him, the [[2007 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]]. He threw for two touchdowns and 204 yards, completing 10 of 18 pass attempts with just one [[interception]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Cleveland Browns – September 30th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709300cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Browns would later beat the Ravens again, making it the first time since 2001 that the Browns were able to sweep the Ravens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Baltimore Ravens – November 18th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711180rav.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 13 of the 2007 season, the Browns faced the [[2007 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. Down 27–21 late in the 4th, the Browns drove down to the Cardinals 34-yard line. On fourth down, Anderson threw a pass to the end zone which was caught by [[Kellen Winslow II]]. The pass was ruled out of bounds and held up through review. Anderson argued that Winslow was forced out, but the force-out rule was not reviewable. The game was notable for the officials' missed call of a [[Braylon Edwards]] catch and tackle by contact, but mistakenly ruled a touchdown as Edwards got up and ran to the endzone.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Arizona Cardinals – December 2nd, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200712020crd.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Another close game that could have put the Browns in the playoffs was December 23 against the Bengals, in which the Browns went scoreless in the first half, but held the Bengals scoreless in the second half. Anderson had four interceptions, two of them on consecutive plays, and one more in the Cincinnati end zone as Cleveland appeared to be heading for a scoring drive. The Browns also had two turnover-on-downs possessions. Anderson threw two touchdown passes to [[Braylon Edwards]], Cleveland's only scores in the game. The game ended in a 19–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Cincinnati Bengals – December 23rd, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200712230cin.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Anderson led the Browns to a 10–6 overall record, 10–5 in games in which he started.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Anderson 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeDe00/gamelog/2007 |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 Cleveland Browns Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/2007.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Anderson finished with 29 touchdowns to 19 interceptions. During the week of December 12–18, Anderson was named as a first alternate for the [[2008 Pro Bowl]] at quarterback.<ref name=Edwards_Cribbs_headed_to_Hawaii>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Zac |date=December 18, 2007 |title=Edwards, Cribbs headed to Hawaii |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=7991 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071221121615/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=7991 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=December 21, 2007 |access-date=December 19, 2007 |website=clevelandbrowns.com}}</ref> On February 4, [[Tom Brady]] announced he would not be attending the Pro Bowl due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2008 |title=Anderson replaces Brady in Pro Bowl, Winslow also going to Hawaii |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=3230289 |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> This paved the way for Anderson to make his first and only appearance in the Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/probowl.htm |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The PFWA named Anderson as their Most Improved Player.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PFWA Most Improved Player Winners |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/pfwa-most-improved-player-award.htm |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2008 season====
On February 29, 2008, the first day of free agency, after speculation that Anderson would leave Cleveland to pursue a bigger contract, Anderson agreed to a $27 million, three-year contract to stay with the Browns through the 2010 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson, Zac |date=February 29, 2008 |title=Browns, Anderson agree to terms |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=8245 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080305201317/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/article.php?id=8245 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=March 5, 2008 |access-date=February 29, 2008}}</ref> The contract made Anderson one of the highest paid players in the NFL, However, Cleveland fans were split between the proven Anderson and the locally-homegrown Quinn (an image of Quinn wearing a [[Bernie Kosar]] jersey as a kid was shown at the [[2007 NFL draft]]), many were speculating if the Browns were in a similar position the [[San Diego Chargers]] were in a few years back with [[Drew Brees]] and their first-round pick [[Philip Rivers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Withers |first=Tom |date=October 26, 2007 |title=Browns GM Savage pleased with start, encouraged by progress - USATODAY.com |url=https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/football/2007-10-26-3379455050_x.htm |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=usatoday30.usatoday.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

The 2008 season was a tough one for the Browns and Anderson. In the preseason, he suffered a concussion when he was sacked by [[Osi Umenyiora]] of the New York Giants. This would prevent him from practicing for the majority of the preseason. In the season opener against the [[2008 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], he was 11-of-24 for 110 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Cleveland Browns – September 7th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809070cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On November 3, after starting out the season the Browns announced that Anderson would be benched in favor of Quinn. On November 23, during a game against the [[2008 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Quinn was benched by Crennel in favor of Anderson. On November 25, Quinn was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a broken finger and Anderson was renamed the starting quarterback. On November 30, Anderson was injured during a game versus the [[2008 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Cleveland Browns – November 30th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811300cle.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> It was later revealed to be an MCL injury, which put Anderson out for the season. [[Ken Dorsey]] came into the starting role, but could not save the Browns. The Browns lost the last four games to finish with a 4–12 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 Cleveland Browns Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/2008.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2009 season====
In the 2009 season, Anderson continued to compete with Quinn. He appeared in eight games for the Browns. He finished with 888 passing yards, three touchdowns, and ten interceptions. The Browns finished the season with a 5–11 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Cleveland Browns Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/2009.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Anderson 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeDe00/gamelog/2009 |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Anderson would wind up being one of the most productive quarterbacks for Cleveland, statistically, and that legacy lasted over the franchise's next nine years as he ranked the third-best quarterback overall between 2000 and 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McManamon |first=Pat |date=April 13, 2018 |title=Ranking the Browns' 28 QBs since 1999 from worst to first |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/23139554/ranking-browns-28-qbs-1999-worst-first |access-date=March 18, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
[[File:Derek Anderson on sidelines in 2010.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Anderson with the Cardinals in 2010]]
On March 17, 2010, Anderson signed a two-year deal worth $7.25 million with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2010 |title=Derek Anderson signs two-year deal with Cardinals |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2010-mar-17-la-sp-newswire-20100318-story.html |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> After [[Kurt Warner]] retired and [[Matt Leinart]] was released, Anderson became the starting quarterback for the Cardinals. After struggling in his first few games, Anderson was benched in favor of rookie [[Max Hall (American football)|Max Hall]] on October 6.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Anderson 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeDe00/gamelog/2010 |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Anderson was named the starting quarterback again for the November 7 game against the [[2010 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] after Hall struggled.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biggs |first=Brad |date=November 4, 2010 |title=Cardinals turn back to Derek Anderson |url=http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Cardinals-turn-back-to-Derek-Anderson.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101107182551/http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Cardinals-turn-back-to-Derek-Anderson.html |archive-date=November 7, 2010 |access-date=November 7, 2010 |website=nationalfootballpost.com}}</ref> However, in week 14 he suffered a concussion in the Cardinals 43–13 win over the Broncos. Anderson was replaced with Hall in that game, whose season ended with a separated shoulder later in the game. Rookie [[John Skelton (American football)|John Skelton]] finished the game and succeeded Anderson as the Cardinals' starting quarterback. Skelton suffered in the same fashion, as the Cardinals went 1 and 2 in the last three games of the season. The last game was a 39–7 stomping by the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Anderson also created a notable soundbite after being caught on national TV laughing with teammate [[Deuce Lutui]] while his team was playing poorly. His subsequent anger toward the reporter who kept questioning him on the subject made national news and was featured on several sports shows.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 30, 2010 |title=Derek Anderson sounds off after game |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5865332 |access-date=March 14, 2013 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Running back [[Tim Hightower]] defended Anderson after the incident, and Anderson apologized for the misstep.<ref>{{cite web |title=Derek Anderson apologizes for rant |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/derek-anderson-apologizes-for-rant |work=FOX Sports |access-date=23 July 2025}}</ref>
Anderson was released by the Cardinals on July 28, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=July 28, 2011 |title=Release Tracker |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/release-tracker |access-date=July 29, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Talk]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 Arizona Cardinals Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/crd/2010.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
Anderson signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on July 31, 2011. He served as the backup to quarterback [[Cam Newton]] and played only a few times for Carolina either to end the game or play for an injured Newton.

On September 7, 2014, Anderson made his first start since 2010 after Newton suffered an injury which held him out. In the game, Anderson completed 24 of 34 passes for 230 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions, leading the Panthers to a 20–14 victory over the [[2014 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – September 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070tam.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Anderson would have his second start of the season after Newton was involved in a car accident, coincidentally also against the Buccaneers. Anderson finished the game by completing 25 of 40 passes for 277 yards, a touchdown, and no interceptions, helping the Panthers win 19–17.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers – December 14th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412140car.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On February 7, 2016, Anderson was part of the Panthers team that played in [[Super Bowl 50]]. In the game, Anderson served as Cam Newton's active-backup as the Panthers fell to the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] by a score of 24–10.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl 50 – Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers – February 7th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm |access-date=September 2, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>
[[File:Derek Anderson Panthers at Ravens 2016 preseason (cropped).jpg|thumb|Anderson with the Panthers in 2016]]
In Week 4 of the 2016 season against the [[2016 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], Anderson entered the game after an injury to Newton and threw for 172 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions as the Panthers lost by a score of 48–33.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strickland |first=Bryan |date=October 2, 2016 |title=Derek Anderson almost pulls it out |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/derek-anderson-almost-pulls-it-out-17805898 |access-date=January 1, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> Due to Newton's injury, Anderson started the Week 5 game against the Buccaneers and threw for 278 yards and two interceptions as the Panthers lost by a score of 17–14.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Max |date=October 10, 2016 |title=Turnovers tarnish Derek Anderson's night |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Turnovers-tarnish-Derek-Andersons-night/99123548-30fb-4292-b3d6-313b6f73013d |access-date=January 1, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> In Week 13 against the [[2016 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], Anderson made his second start of the season since Newton had violated the team's dress code. He threw an interception on the Panthers' first play on offense and was then replaced by Newton.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joseph |first=Andrew |date=December 4, 2016 |title=The Panthers surprisingly started Derek Anderson for one play and it went terribly |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/12/carolina-panthers-start-derek-anderson-cam-newton-seahawks-nfl |access-date=January 1, 2017 |website=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Lindsay H. |date=December 5, 2016 |title=Cam Newton explains dress code violation that led to benching |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/panthers/2016/12/04/cam-newton-benched-derek-anderson-start-carolina-ron-rivera/94977530/ |access-date=January 1, 2017 |website=USA Today}}</ref> Anderson came into the 2017 NFC [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: New Orleans Saints 31, Carolina Panthers 26|Wild Card Round]] on January 7, 2018, against the [[2017 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] in the fourth quarter after Newton went down with an injury. He had one pass attempt in the 31–26 defeat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints – January 7th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801070nor.htm |access-date=January 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
On October 7, 2018, it was announced Anderson would sign with the [[Buffalo Bills]], reuniting with [[Sean McDermott]] and [[Brandon Beane]] from his days playing for the [[Carolina Panthers]], to serve as backup and mentor to rookie quarterback [[Josh Allen]]. The Bills completed the transaction on October 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=October 9, 2018 |title=Bills sign veteran QB Derek Anderson |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-veteran-qb-derek-anderson |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

On October 17, following an injury to Allen and a poor performance by backup quarterback [[Nathan Peterman]] in relief, Anderson was named the Week 7 starter for the Bills against the [[2018 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=October 17, 2018 |title=Derek Anderson starting for Bills with Josh Allen out |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/derek-anderson-starting-for-bills-with-josh-allen-out-0ap3000000975241 |access-date=October 17, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> During the game, Anderson threw for 175 yards, no touchdowns, and three interceptions in a 37–5 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harding |first=Robert |date=October 22, 2018 |title=Buffalo Bills Week 7 Report Card: Colts stampede Anderson, Bills 37–5 |url=https://auburnpub.com/blogs/in_the_pros/buffalo-bills-week-report-card-colts-stampede-anderson-bills/article_c431395c-d555-11e8-b3f7-1b8718ee4c6f.html |access-date=January 23, 2019 |website=Auburn Citizen |language=en}}</ref> With Allen still injured, Anderson made the start the following week against the [[2018 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. He threw for 290 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception before leaving the game in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=October 30, 2018 |title=Patriots win 25–6 as Derek Anderson leaves late with injury |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/patriots-win-25-6-as-derek-anderson-leaves-late-with-injury |access-date=January 23, 2019 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en}}</ref> He was put into concussion protocol and ruled out for the Week 9 game against the [[2018 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], and Peterman was named the starter once again.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 26, 2018 |title=Bills' Derek Anderson: Remains in concussion protocol |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bills-derek-anderson-remains-in-concussion-protocol-402853/ |access-date=January 23, 2019 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 31, 2018, Anderson signed a one-year contract extension with the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=December 31, 2018 |title=Bills sign Derek Anderson for 2019 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bills-sign-derek-anderson-for-2019 |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On May 9, 2019, Anderson announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dubin |first=Jared |date=May 9, 2019 |title=Bills announce retirement of Derek Anderson, who once upon a time won 10 games for the Browns |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/bills-announce-retirement-of-derek-anderson-who-once-upon-a-time-won-10-games-for-the-browns/ |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> He later attributed his retirement to lingering effects from the 2018 concussion; he remains in regular contact with Allen and approved of the hiring of his (Anderson's) friend [[Ken Dorsey]] as quarterbacks coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Capaccio |first=Sal |date=August 22, 2019 |title=Derek Anderson reflects on his time with Bills |url=https://www.audacy.com/wgr550/articles/news/derek-anderson-reflects-his-time-bills |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=www.audacy.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Anderson and his wife Mallory have three children.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://littlesous.com/resources-sub/lifestyle/in-the-kitchen-with-nfl-veteran-derek-anderson|title=In the Kitchen with NFL Veteran Derek Anderson|website=Little Sous|access-date=September 21, 2026}}</ref>

He enjoys golfing, where he sometimes plays to a [[Handicap (golf)|plus handicap]]. Anderson has also dabbled in [[Caddie|caddying]]; in April 2025, he caddied for friend and [[PGA Tour]] pro [[Kevin Chappell]] in the [[Zurich Classic of New Orleans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cunningham |first=Kevin |date=2025-05-11 |title=Why caddying on PGA Tour shook this NFL QB |url=https://golf.com/news/why-caddying-pga-tour-shook-nfl-qb-stressful/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=Golf |language=en-US}}</ref>
